Promising location, very disappointing beer
Oct 2019
This is one of the larger and more attractive venues in central 'Old Town' area, and usually not too crowded - unlike the heaving bar strip of Ta Hien which is immediately adjacent.

Unfortunately, their self-brewed beers are really pretty awful - slightly flat, and without any great depth or variety of flavour. Really, I tried almost all of them over a couple of visits, and it was very difficult to discern any significant difference between most of them - even completely different varieties. The only one I found reasonably palatable was one they had in bottle only, which was supposedly flavoured with pho soup spices (I didn't actually get the pho-ness of it, but it was novel, and quite pleasant).

Service (as in most places in Hanoi, unfortunately) was decidedly minimal; staff seem to wish they were somewhere else, and engage with you as little as possible.

Great selection of local craft beers
Aug 2019
The C-brewmaster brewery was founded only in 2016, and the craft beer scene is still developing, so its not surprise that it’s a bit hit and miss. Some beers are great and some are…not. This is one of their flagship pubs, you can try tried and tested flavours (Stout, IPA etc) as well as local flavours like Cool mint ale, Pho essence ale, or Liquorice stout ale! 
There is a bit of inconsistency in the serving temperature, not always served as they should be, additionally in this heat the beer gets warm really quickly. I would chill the beer a little bit more. Food was a cut above the usual pub grub, especially the pork schnitzel which was lovely..moist, tasty and crunchy, we thoroughly enjoyed it.

winter

Very inconsistent
Jul 2019 • Couples
If you’re only visiting Hanoi for a short time, this is the place you’ll most likely stumble across yourself. C-Brew is located in the absolute heart of Hanoi’s nightlife area. There is plenty of seating, especially upstairs where you can sit on the balcony and watch the street traffic come and go. There are around 8 beers on tap, and around 25-30 bottled offerings…. Wow. By far the biggest range of beers in Vietnam. Several of the beers come only in larger bottles, with significantly higher process, so I didn’t get the chance to sample these. Choosing a beer was a little hard, as nearly all the beers, with maybe only 2-3 exceptions had IBU (International Bitterness Units) of under 20… a little odd. I counted no less than five pale ale’s, all with a near identical IBU, so this made choosing one difficult. I tried one that stood out from the pack, a mint pale ale. I got a glass of yeasty sourness with a hint of toothpaste. Round two was an amber ale on tap, which was significantly better. 
Update: Due to such a mixed feeling and the huge variety of beers I didn’t try, I decided to give C-Brew a second go. I had the Mad King Pale Ale, Pho Essence Ale, and the Papa Triple IPA. Let's start off with the good. The pale was quite good, no problems there. The triple… claimed to have an IBU of about 60. Simply put, it wasn’t, 30 at best, and that’s being generous. Honestly, it didn’t smell or taste much like an IPA at all. And the Pho Essence was dead flat right out of the bottle. I complained but was told that that’s how the beer was supposed to be. So I persevered and found the beer was frankly undrinkable. I complained again and received a fresh bottle, which thankfully was carbonated. Still not a great beer, but a definite improvement. Interestingly, the flat beer was a more recent batch than the properly carbonated one!
All up, I would have to describe C-Brew as inconsistent. There are good beers to be had, but a lot of bad ones too. I can't even imagine what some of the more experimental beers would be like, such as the mulberry ale or whiskey beer. Maybe this is another case of beers being suited more towards local tastes, but generally speaking, I didn’t enjoy C-Brew beers, and even those I did were just ok.

One of the best craft beer bars in Vietnam
Jun 2019 • Couples
So much choice in beer and such a reasonable price compared to the other craft breweries, around 80k per bottle and 55k for a draught beer.
Beers were amazing, super flavourful, me and my partner tried quite a few, only one we didn't like was the lemon grass one but the rest were amazing!
Good selection of bar snacks/nibbles, we had some sesame sweet potatoes which were great, they also do homemade beef jerky. They have a full menu of other food but it didn't look that great, so I'd just go for the beers! 
Loved being able to people watch from the doorway, we went back a few times, favourite bar in Hanoi.
